methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $31M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
TerraDepth is a Series C–stage transportation company that has raised $31.1M to date. The valuation universe consists of eight private frontier-tech peers in transportation, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia; no public comparables exist in a sufficiently narrow peer set.

A stage-progression method was applied, using the $31.1M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage progression. This yields an implied valuation of $53M. A peer-median approach was not applicable: while three same-sector peers exist in the broader transportation universe, zero companies met the narrow filters of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation-tier classification. Drawing a median from the broader, unfiltered peer set would lack sufficient statistical rigor and introduce material bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $45M (low) to $61M (high), with a median point of $53M. Given the single-method foundation and the absence of peer triangulation, the primary uncertainty centers on whether the 1.7x multiplier accurately reflects TerraDepth's specific risk profile and capital efficiency relative to frontier-transportation norms. Validation would benefit from closer inspection of growth trajectory, unit economics, and competitive positioning within the narrower subset of relevant peers.
